title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16
abstract: arXiv:2610.32229v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscill

translated_title: 用MXFP4训练MoE大语言模型：我们如何缩小与BF16的差距
translated_abstract: 以低于8比特的精度算术训练大语言模型（LLM）有望在内存带宽和计算吞吐量方面带来显著收益，然而FP4格式引入的量化误差非常严重，若不加处理足以破坏优化的稳定性。我们提出了ALTO，一个开源的训练方案，用于在MLPerf Small MoE Training基准上以MXFP4微缩放格式训练GPT-OSS-20B——一个拥有200亿参数的混合专家模型。该方案将Abecassis、Felix等人[arXiv:2509.25149]的成熟技术（混合1D/2D块量化、随机Hadamard变换和随机舍入）与从TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]改进而来的简化权重去振荡方案相结合。在全局批大小为16的C4验证集上，MXFP4 + RHT + SR + 去振荡的组合在16,128步时达到3.3350的验证损失，仅比BF16基线（3.3283）高0.007，相比未使用去振荡的MXFP4，弥补了约50%的差距。
tldr: 该论文提出ALTO开源训练方案，通过结合混合1D/2D块量化、随机Hadamard变换、随机舍入与简化的权重去振荡技术，使200亿参数MoE模型GPT-OSS-20B在MXFP4低精度格式下训练的验证损失仅比BF16基线高0.007，大幅缩小了FP4训练与BF16全精度训练之间的差距。
en_tdlr: ALTO is an open-source training recipe that combines hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, stochastic rounding, and a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme, enabling the 20B-parameter MoE model GPT-OSS-20B to be trained in MXFP4 with validation loss only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline, closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation.
